To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

visibly pushdown languages are: - a robust class of languages, closed under all basic operations, - tractable and decidable, - a class of languages that is expressive enough to model program properties, - and that is closed under complementation, intersection and renaming.

the class of visibly context-free languages is closed under all Boolean operations, that it can be characterized by the MSO theory of words with a binary matching relation, that it can also be characterized by regular tree languages, and that it can be used to verify recursive programs with respect context-free properties.

(1) the class of visibly context-free languages is closed under all Boolean operations and Kleene-*. (2) the class is robust: it can be characterized in terms of a logic, in terms of a tree language, and in terms of an automata model (deterministic Büchi automata).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a class of languages that combines the expressiveness of context-free languages and the tractability of regular languages.
the study of visibly pushdown automaton and languages, which we view as a natural extension of regular languages and automata.
extending the theory and applications of regular languages to the realm of context-free languages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class of visibly context-free languages is the class of context-free languages with the most robust and well-behaved closure properties.
the class VPL of visibly pushdown (regular) languages is the right class of regular languages for program analysis.

the class of visibly context-free languages is a robust and natural extension of regular languages, which is rich enough to handle many program analysis questions, and yet is tractably decidable and amenable to efficient algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the class VPL is the class of context free languages that are robust enough to be closed under complementation and that is rich enough so that many interesting problems are decidable in Exptime.
we introduce a new class of languages that is robust, tractable and rich enough to model many program analysis problems.
the class VPL of languages is a robust class, and it is the class of languages that are definable in MSO with the matching predicate, or in MSO with an additional stack predicate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the class VPL is the right level of expressivity between regular languages and context-free languages for program analysis and verification.
the class of visibly languages is a rich and tractable class of languages that can be used as a basis for the design of static program analysis tools.
the class of visibly languages is a robust, tractable and natural class that captures many of the program analysis questions that have been studied in the literature.
